prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1300; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed the first notice of loss for a left-turn collision at an intersection. Insured reports being struck by oncoming vehicle while turning left on a green arrow. Police report requested. Claimant has retained counsel, who has asked that all contact go through their office.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office to confirm representation and receive the initial demand package. Counsel reports neck and back strain with ongoing physical therapy. Medical records authorization requested. No recorded statement will be taken from the claimant directly.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report. Officer notes the other driver was traveling straight through the intersection and the signal phase is consistent with the insured's account. Witness statement from a nearby pedestrian is on file. Liability appears to lean toward the other driver, pending review of photos and vehicle damage.

Entry 4: Received preliminary medical documentation from claimant's counsel showing evaluation for cervical and lumbar strain. Treatment plan includes chiropractic sessions and home exercise. Reviewed records for consistency with the reported mechanism of injury. Bodily injury reserve adjusted upward. Flagged file for supervisor review given attorney involvement.

Entry 5: Followed up with defense counsel regarding the insured's coverage position and the claimant's pending demand. Requested updated treatment notes and billing ledger before evaluating settlement range. Diary set for follow-up in thirty days. Insured has been kept informed of progress and reminded to forward any correspondence received directly.
